title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§10-15 of the chapter 'De diametris apparentibus motuque horario vero solis ac lunae, in eclipsibus lunaribus'). Euler has written the ratio of the moon's true motion to its mean motion, dφ/du, as a trigonometric series. Here φ is true longitude and u is the mean (anomalistic) motion. The arguments are v, the moon's eccentric anomaly counted from apogee; V, the sun's anomaly; and η, the elongation moon minus sun. The page finishes the numerical series begun on p.388. Its terms are: 0.000006 cos4η, 0.000004 cos(η−v), 0.001502 cos(2η−2v), −0.000328 cos(2η+v), −0.020979 cos(2η−v) (evection), −0.000524 cos(2η+V), −0.000649 cos(2η−V), 0.000365 cos(2η−v+V) and 0.000209 cos(2η−v−V). Each coefficient carries its tabular log (characteristic +10).

Hourly series. Multiplying by the hourly mean anomalistic motion du = 32'39.8" = 1959.8" (13.065°/24h) gives the true hourly motion in arcseconds. Logs are added to log du = 3.292212. Terms under about 1" are dropped. The result is:
33'3" − 216 cos v + 9 cos2v − cos η + 40 cos2η + 3 cos(2η−2v) − 41 cos(2η−v) − cos(2η+V) − cos(2η−V).
Euler remarks that this is far easier than the usual practice of computing two lunar places an hour apart and differencing them.

§13, empirical calibration. Euler distrusts the constant α, which collects many small contributions from the denominator. He therefore tests the formula against the tables over one hour starting from v = u = η = 0, V = 90°. After the hour, v = 1858.6", u = 1959.8" and η = 1627" (that is, the moon's hourly motion less the sun's ~148"). The tables give 1774.7"; the formula gives 1775.7". He lowers the constant by 1" to 33'2".

Specialisation to the syzygies.
- Conjunction (η = 0): all η-terms collapse to functions of v and V. Hourly motion = 33'40.8" − 258.3 cos v + 11.7 cos2v − 1.8 cos V + 1.4 cos(v−V).
- Opposition (η = 180°): only the cos η term changes sign, so the constant becomes 33'43.1".
- The N cos v term is omitted, being absorbable into the eccentricity.

§14, extreme cases.
- Apogee (v = 0): conjunction 29'34.2" − 0.4 cos V; opposition 29'36.5" − 0.4 cos V.
- Perigee (v = 180°): conjunction 38'10.8" − 3.2 cos V; opposition 38'13.1" − 3.2 cos V.

Purpose: tabulating the moon's true hourly motion for eclipse and occultation computations. The next page proposes a dedicated hourly-motion table.
errors: The conjunction cos v coefficient is printed as 258.3 (log 2.41212). Summing the page's own pieces gives 0.11022 + 0.000328 + 0.020979 − 0.000004 = 0.131523, and ×1959.8 = 257.8" (log 2.4112). On the next page Euler uses 216.4 instead of 216.0 for the cos v term, which gives about 258.1. So there is an unexplained discrepancy of 0.2–0.5", most likely a small arithmetic or revision inconsistency.

Minor inconsistency in the truncation rule. Euler says he omits terms under 1", yet keeps −cos(2η+V) at 1.03" while dropping the ~0.64" cos(2η+v) term. The rule is fine, but the latter term actually contributes about 0.6" to the §13 check.

All other checks agree with the stated coefficients to rounding: the 1983.1" constant, the logs, the §13 test value of about 1775.8", the syzygy constants 2020.8"/2023.1", cos2v 11.7, cos V −1.8, cos(v−V) 1.4, and the §14 values.

ideas.what: Direct trigonometric series for the moon's true hourly motion: dφ/du times the hourly mean motion, with evection, variation and annual-type terms in elongation, anomaly and solar anomaly.
ideas.modern_name: Analytic expression for the lunar velocity (derivative of the longitude series)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in 18th-century lunar theory (Euler, Mayer, Clairaut); horary-motion tables appear in lunar tables of the period
ideas.where_published: Closely related material in Euler's lunar theories E187 (1753) and E418 (1772). This piece is posthumous (Opera postuma 1862).

ideas.what: Empirical correction of the constant term by comparing with a two-place difference computed from tables.
ideas.modern_name: Calibration of an analytic series against ephemeris

ideas.what: Reduction of the hourly-motion series at syzygies (η = 0, 180°) and at apogee/perigee, for eclipse use.
ideas.modern_name: Hourly motion at syzygy for eclipse computation

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine numerical reduction of Euler's own lunar series to an hourly-motion formula, with an empirical 1" calibration. It is internally consistent apart from a sub-arcsecond discrepancy in the cos v coefficient. Nothing here appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Line 2, first log under 0.000006 cos4η should read '4,778' (log 6·10⁻⁶ = 4.778 − 10).
Line 4, log under 0.020979 cos(2η−v) should be '8,32178' (the transcription's '[?],32178' / an apparent '3,32178' is wrong); log 0.020979 = 8.32178 − 10.
Line 5 begins '+ 0,000365 cos(2η − v + V)' and its log is '6,56229' (the leading characters are obscured in the scan).
The first term of the hourly-motion formula is 33'3" (= 1983" = 1.01188 × 1959.8"), consistent with the later correction to 33'2".
The η value in §13 is 1627", consistent with the hourly lunar motion minus the solar hourly motion (~148").
